tools.description: Run ONE command as root on the local host via sudo. sudo works: the user sees the exact argv and your reason in a TUI approval window, confirms and types their sudo password there if sudo asks (passwordless sudo works too). The password never reaches you — never ask for it in chat, put it into a command or use `sudo -S`/`echo … | sudo`. Returns exit_code/stdout/stderr, or an error if the user denied it or authentication failed — then do not retry on your own, ask the user. Never call sudo via shell.exec; never say sudo is impossible while this tool is available.
tools.name: host.sudo_exec

argv.description: Exact argv of the command to run as root, e.g. ["apt-get", "install", "-y", "ripgrep"]. No shell: no pipes, redirections or globbing. Do not include sudo.

reason.description: Short reason shown to the user in the approval window.
